clue.text: Elementary sort of copy

definitions.meaning: a chemical element, so this sense is of the elements
a duplicate made with ... paper is a ... copy, often just called a ...

explanation.surface: Someone describes a basic kind of duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun works as a double meaning: a chemical element, and a copy made with transfer paper.

clue.text: A half-successful lobby

indicators.note: half of the word for successful is used, its first five of ten letters

parts.note: successful means triumphant

explanation.surface: A lobbying campaign that only partly worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a verb for campaigning, but it is the noun for an entrance hall. 'half' takes TRIUM, the first half of TRIUMPHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the central hall or entrance area of a building, a synonym for a lobby.

clue.text: Boys' leader ordered opening of presents during Christmas

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order

indicators.note: during places one piece within another

parts.note: Nowell is an old word for Christmas, as in the carol

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scout leader gave orders to open the presents on Christmas Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal but is a past tense; 'during' places the P from 'opening of presents' within the old carol word for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Boy Scout movement, so he is the boys' leader.

clue.text: Pharisee in province rules problem must be raised

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
a code is a set of rules

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upward, so backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A religious leader in a province faces a rule-bound puzzle that must be brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUM to MUS in this down entry. NI, the Province, is Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee in John's Gospel who visited Jesus by night.

clue.text: Partly lower trousers? What spectacles!

definitions.meaning: to moon is to bare one's bottom
... spectacles are reading glasses with lenses cut flat at the top

explanation.surface: Someone drops their trousers a little, and onlookers exclaim at the sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-moon glasses are a style of spectacles, and mooning halfway is a comic second meaning.

clue.text: Original thinker identifying place of troublesome movement?

parts.note: here names a place, this spot
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a troublesome movement

explanation.surface: A free thinker pinpoints where an unsettling movement began.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs departing from orthodoxy, a thinker of unorthodox, original ideas.

clue.text: Part of body needs one simple garment

parts.note: a lung is a part of the body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A body part requires one plain piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A LUNGI is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a simple wraparound sarong-like garment worn in India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Chap has short hair

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a mane is a long growth of hair

explanation.surface: A man has a short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of MANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal synonym for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Revisions of Tudor period held to be mad

indicators.note: held means one piece is kept inside another
revisions rework the letters of the following word into a new order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Rewriting the history of Tudor times is considered crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revisions of' rearranges the five letters of the king's dynasty as OUTRD, and 'held' puts the period inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Outraged means furious, and mad is a common informal word for angry.

clue.text: He works on programme favouring Mussolini, right?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italy's leader

explanation.surface: A broadcaster backing Mussolini is asked if that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is the person who works on making a television or radio programme.

clue.text: Back in trap, unknown number

indicators.note: back means the short word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: a net is a trap
in algebra, y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Back in the trap, a mysterious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns IN to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, ten times nine.

clue.text: Hooligan inhaling pot has changed

indicators.note: inhaling means taking something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth often seen as a hooligan
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: A thug who has smoked cannabis is a different person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests cannabis, which 'inhaling' supports, but it is an urn. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned is a synonym for changed, as milk turns or a person turns into something else.

clue.text: In fish, left bone — taken to court

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: tuna is a fish
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: Someone who found a bone left in their fish is taking the matter to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits at the front but governs the bone going inside the fish; the left sign follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that judges disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: Reversed round back of bus, cul-de-sac being not accessible

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around others

parts.note: to undo something is to reverse it, so undid means reversed

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a close is a dead-end street, a cul-de-sac

explanation.surface: A bus turned round in a dead end that could not be reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' looks like a reversal signal but is a synonym (undo = reverse); 'round' wraps it around the last letter of bus plus a dead-end street.
explanation.definitionFit: Undisclosed means kept secret, so the information is not accessible.

clue.text: Command fee in translating novel

indicators.note: translating turns words into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order for a fee to be paid for a translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' rearranges the letters of COMMAND FEE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Of Mice and Men is a novella by John Steinbeck, published in 1937.

clue.text: Food, for example, South American country's always ignored

parts.note: as can mean such as, for example

indicators.note: ignored means a piece of the word is left out

parts.note: Paraguay is a South American country, with the possessive S
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Food, such as a South American country is always overlooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes AY from PARAGUAYS, leaving PARAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable eaten as food.

clue.text: Tropical native with money holding a party

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains another

parts.note: cash is money
Lab is short for Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: A local in the tropics who has cash is hosting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the A and the party inside the money, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash is a tree or gourd vine native to tropical regions.

clue.text: In principle, college has first to admit president

indicators.note: first says this part comes before the college
to admit means to let something inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: taken as written
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
Corpus Christi is a college at Oxford and at Cambridge, often called Corpus

explanation.surface: In theory, a college is the first to take a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts Lincoln inside the 'has'; 'first' sets that before the Oxbridge college name.
explanation.definitionFit: Habeas corpus is a legal principle that a detained person must be brought before a court.

clue.text: Arranged to get through border, lying

indicators.note: the answer gets through the words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A plan to cross a frontier by telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get through' signals the letters lying within 'border, lying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means neatly arranged or organised.

clue.text: Have fun, taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means one piece contains another

parts.note: to revel is to have fun

explanation.surface: Enjoy yourself and go to see a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts A inside REVEL. 'show' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show it.

clue.text: Girl ran steadily; but what did Joris and Dirck do?

definitions.text: what did Joris and Dirck do?

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to lope is to run with a steady easy stride

explanation.surface: A girl jogged along, but how did two riders in a poem travel?
explanation.walkthrough: Joris and Dirck ride with the narrator of Browning's poem How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix: 'I galloped, Dirck galloped, we galloped all three'.
explanation.definitionFit: The riders in Browning's poem rode their horses at full speed, the verb the poem repeats.

clue.text: Fighter at Verdun turned up to collect fuel

indicators.note: to collect means one piece gathers another inside it
turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A soldier at the Battle of Verdun came back to pick up fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives PU, and 'to collect' puts the fuel inside it. Verdun was the great French battle of 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: A poilu was a French infantry soldier of the First World War, like those at Verdun.

clue.text: Tool for gardener that's sort of blind

definitions.meaning: a heavy rolling cylinder used to flatten a lawn
a window blind that winds round a rod

explanation.surface: A gardening implement that can also screen a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a garden lawn tool and a type of window blind take this name, from rolling.

clue.text: Censors feature for radio, bringing outcry in Japan

indicators.note: for radio means the words are said aloud as on air

parts.note: to ban something is to censor it, so censors means bans; an eye is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Censorship of a radio programme provokes a protest in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for radio' says BANS EYE is heard, sounding like the Japanese cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Banzai is a Japanese cheer or battle cry, a shout heard in Japan.

clue.text: Energy to get closer

definitions.meaning: a fastener that closes a garment

explanation.surface: Gaining energy to come nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is both liveliness and a zipper, a device that closes clothes.

clue.text: Regret one's damaged part of our paper

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are broken up into a new order

parts.note: one is gives I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that part of the newspaper got damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges REGRET plus IS. The Times prints a Register column of births, marriages and deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: The Register is a section of The Times, the paper where this clue appeared.

clue.text: Cuts of meat, high-class to look at, shortly put into dish

parts.note: chops are cuts of meat
U means upper-class in British usage

indicators.note: shortly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Cuts of meat, upmarket in appearance, are quickly put into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts EYE to EY. U for upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop suey is a Chinese-style dish of stir-fried meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Leathery piece of lamb?

parts.note: reads as a tough bit of meat, but means a leather seat, which is also a cut of lamb

explanation.surface: A tough bit of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a leather riding seat and also a joint of lamb from the back.
